I'm 58 years old. Never went to school, can't read a word, but I've been farming these 9 mu for 30 years since my father passed. My son works in a factory in Handan and sends some money home. My wife and I do most of the field work. Some family members work off-farm, so hands are tight when cotton needs picking.

I have 9 mu total. Six mu I plant cotton — that's been my main crop for 20 years, it's where the cash comes from. The other 3 mu I put winter wheat in last October, same as always. After I cut the wheat in early June, I'll plant maize right away — no time to waste, maybe five or six days between harvest and planting, so I can't do much tillage.

For the cotton, I plant around April 20th when the soil feels warm enough. I use my own saved seed — why pay when I have good seed from last year? I just buy a little new seed every few years to refresh. Before planting I plow once with my small tractor and put down about half a bag of compound fertilizer per mu — the 15-15-15 stuff. Lao Zhang at the supply store weighs it for me, about 25 kg per mu I think. When the cotton starts flowering in July, I topdress with urea, about 15 kg per mu. I irrigate twice — once after planting if there's no rain, and once when it flowers. Water from the well costs electricity money, so I don't waste it. For pests, I spray when I see bollworms. Usually three or four times with insecticide, and I put herbicide down before planting. Cotton needs lots of hands. My wife and I do the planting, weeding, and spraying. For picking in September and October, I hire two or three women from the village for about twelve days total — my back isn't what it used to be and we can't pick 6 mu by ourselves. I expect around 220 kg of lint per mu, about the same as my neighbors if the weather is normal.

The wheat is already in the ground. I topdressed it in March with urea when it greened up — about 20 kg per mu. I'll irrigate it twice more before June. Should get about 400 kg per mu if no late frost or drought.

For the maize, I buy fresh hybrid seed every year after wheat harvest — costs about 40 yuan per mu. I put fertilizer down with the seed, about 25 kg compound and 10 kg urea per mu, then topdress once when it's knee-high. One irrigation should be enough if the summer rains come. I grow it for family food and chicken feed. Maize is easier than cotton.

Money is tight. Cotton needs the most cash — fertilizer, pesticide, water, hired pickers. The wheat and maize don't need much more now. All together I need about 3,600 yuan this year for inputs. My son helps with some. I watch every yuan. Last year cotton price was okay, not great. I don't take big risks — I do what worked before. If I spend too much on fertilizer and the price drops, my family loses. Better to be a little careful.
